summary: Ukraine plans to purchase 200,000 mid-range drones by year-end with Western allies providing half, while Russian airstrikes have destroyed 200 of Ukraine's 5,000 gas stations over the past month. Czech President Petr Pavel stated Ukraine has two months to end the war before potential Russian general mobilization post-September elections. Russian tactical aviation launched guided aerial bombs in Kharkiv and Dnipro regions, with drone activity reported across northern and eastern frontlines.
key_points: Ukraine plans to purchase 200,000 mid-range drones by year-end, with Western allies providing half and 20 effective units each receiving 200 million UAH (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31503).
Russian airstrikes have destroyed 200 of Ukraine's 5,000 gas stations over the past month (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31486).
Czech President Petr Pavel stated Ukraine has two months to end the war before potential Russian general mobilization post-September State Duma elections (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31504).
Russian tactical aviation launched guided aerial bombs in Kharkiv region targeting Slatyne and northern areas (Source: @kpszsu/67918).
Drone activity reported in Chernihiv region with two drones heading toward Gorodnya (Source: @eRadarrua/100420).
Ukraine confirmed continued strikes on Russian ships in open waters under UN self-defense rights, following drone incident near Lefkada (Source: @UkraineNow/82526).
Slovenian parliament voted against €44 million military aid transfer to Ukraine, citing domestic needs (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31510).

sections.threat_assessment: Russian escalation includes increased tactical aviation operations with guided aerial bombs across multiple regions, drone activity targeting critical infrastructure, and potential general mobilization following September elections. Ukrainian drone procurement and missile production delays may impact defensive capabilities. Russian airstrikes on energy infrastructure indicate strategic targeting of civilian assets to degrade Ukrainian resistance capacity.
sections.regional_response: NATO summit in Ankara showed divided European responses to Ukrainian requests, with Slovenia rejecting military aid transfers. Estonian proposal to strip IOC of EU funding over Russia's sports return reflects growing European consensus on maintaining sanctions. Polish far-right party leader purchased medical supplies for Russian army, highlighting domestic political divisions in NATO member states.
sections.intelligence_notes: Lviv mass protests erupted after military commissar assaulted a man, identified as local martial arts coach Roman Udut (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31492). Fake photo used as evidence in Volhynia tragedy controversy was actually 1923 psychiatric literature image (Source: @UkraineNow/82528). Russian FSB reported dismantling fraud ring involving over 50 individuals helping Ukrainian scammers (Source: @tass_agency/384629).
